## Das ABC (The alphabet)

`de-DE.lit-de.alphabet` teaches `lit-de.letters.alphabet` in de-DE, klasse-1. Ages 6-7, about 10 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

The ABC as a fixed order, once all letters are known. Lesson 1: the 26 letters in order, which letter comes before or after another, a gap in a run of letters; the child says the ABC aloud in parts (speak tasks, practice only). Lesson 2 orders words by their first letter, with word cards and with pictures whose words the child hears, finds the word that fits between two others, and ends with the skill check. Ordering by the second and third letter is the next skill (alphabet-order).

## Silben lesen (Reading syllables)

`de-DE.lit-de.blend-syllables` teaches `lit-de.decoding.blend-syllables` in de-DE, klasse-1. Ages 6-7, about 10 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

Children push two sounds together into a syllable (mmm and aaa make Ma) using only the letters they know: L, O, A and M. Lesson 1 reads open syllables (Ma, Mo, La, Lo): hear and find them, fill the missing vowel, spot them among other cards. Lesson 2 reads syllables that start with a vowel (Al, Om, Am), then joins two syllables into the first words (Ma-ma, O-ma, La-ma) and ends with the skill check.

## Groß oder klein? (Capital or small letter?)

`de-DE.lit-de.capital-nouns` teaches `lit-de.spelling.capital-nouns` in de-DE, klasse-1. Ages 6-7, about 10 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

Children write Nomen and the first word of a sentence with a capital letter. Lesson 1 finds the Nomen inside sentences with the Begleiter test (can der, die or das go in front?) and picks the capital or small first letter for a word in a sentence. Lesson 2 adds the start of a sentence: the first word is always written big, also after a Punkt, even when it is not a Nomen; it finds every word that needs a capital in a sentence written all small, and ends with the skill check.

## Sätze abschreiben (Copying sentences)

`de-DE.lit-de.copy-sentences` teaches `lit-de.handwriting.copy-sentences` in de-DE, klasse-1. Ages 6-7, about 11 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

Children copy short sentences without mistakes, with the same Abschreiben steps as for words: read, remember, write, compare. A sentence needs three more things than a word: a gap a finger wide between the words, a capital letter at the start and a Punkt at the end. Lesson 1 copies three-word sentences word by word; lesson 2 remembers two words at a time, checks copies for all three things and ends with the skill check. The app does not yet compare the child's strokes with the model, so the writing tasks are practice and the check rests on the compare, remember and order tasks.

## Wörter abschreiben (Copying words)

`de-DE.lit-de.copy-words` teaches `lit-de.handwriting.copy-words` in de-DE, klasse-1. Ages 6-7, about 10 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

Children copy words without mistakes by the Abschreiben steps a class learns: read the word, remember it, write it from memory, then compare. They copy words onto writing lines, keep a flashed word in mind and pick its spelling, and check a copy against the model. Lesson 1 copies syllable by syllable (So-fa, Do-se); lesson 2 remembers whole words with double letters (Tasse, Sonne, Kanne) and ends with the skill check. The app does not yet compare the child's strokes with the model, so the writing tasks are practice and the check rests on the compare and remember tasks.

## Kurze Sätze nach Diktat (Short sentences from dictation)

`de-DE.lit-de.dictation-short` teaches `lit-de.spelling.dictation-short` in de-DE, klasse-1. Ages 6-7, about 11 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

Children write short practised sentences they hear, with the steps of a class Diktat: listen to the whole sentence, say it again, write it word by word while speaking along, then check it (Anfang groß, Nomen groß, Lücken, Punkt). Lesson 1 takes three-word sentences (Oma ist da.); lesson 2 takes longer ones with a Nomen inside (Der Hund ist im Haus.) and ends with the skill check. The app cannot yet read free writing, so the child builds the heard sentence from word cards, fills its gaps, picks its spelling and finds the mistake in a written copy.

## Gefühle benennen (Naming feelings)

`de-DE.lit-de.feelings` teaches `lit-de.speaking.feelings` in de-DE, klasse-1. Ages 6-7, about 10 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

Naming five feelings (fröhlich, traurig, wütend, ängstlich, müde) and saying how you or someone in a story feels. Lesson 1 learns the words with faces, matches face and word, and finds the feeling that fits a short scene; lesson 2 says it in a sentence with ich bin and weil, uses a more exact word than schlecht, says anger in words instead of hitting, follows a feeling that changes in a story, and ends with the skill check. Speak tasks let the child say how someone feels and compare with the model; they are practice only.

## Erste Sätze lesen (Reading first sentences)

`de-DE.lit-de.first-sentences` teaches `lit-de.decoding.first-sentences` in de-DE, klasse-1. Ages 6-7, about 10 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

Reading a short sentence to the end and finding the picture that fits. Lesson 1: one sentence of three to five words; the last word decides (Der Ball ist rot, Hier sind drei Eier), so the child reads every word before choosing; the child also builds a sentence from word cards. Lesson 2: sentences that differ in one word (Hund, Mund), two sentences that only together name a thing (Es ist gelb. Es ist am Himmel.), and checking a sentence against a picture; it ends with the skill check. Words use only letters taught so far (up to Eu, Ch and J) and the first sight words. The voice never reads the sentence the child has to read.

## Erste Texte lesen (Reading first texts)

`de-DE.lit-de.first-texts` teaches `lit-de.decoding.first-texts` in de-DE, klasse-1. Ages 6-7, about 12 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

Reading a short text of three to four sentences and answering questions about it. Lesson 1: the answer stands in one sentence; the question word (wer, was, wo, wie viele) says what to look for, and the child goes back to the text to find it. Lesson 2: reading more carefully, where a text names more than one thing of a kind (gern and heute, Papa and Ida) and where a statement has to be checked word by word against the text; it ends with the skill check on a new text. All texts are written for Twist; the voice asks the question but never reads the text.

## Die passende Überschrift (The right heading)

Finding the heading that fits a short text. ## Mit Sprache spielen (Playing with language)

`de-DE.lit-de.language-play` teaches `lit-de.vocabulary.language-play` in de-DE, klasse-1. Ages 6-7, about 10 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

Playing with words and sounds. Lesson 1 tells real words from Quatschwörter, finds the Quatschsatz, swaps the first sound of a word to make a new one (Maus, Haus) and makes up Quatschreime; lesson 2 swaps the syllables of a word (Hase, Seha), turns a Quatschwort back into the real word, swaps the parts of a compound and sees the meaning change (Baumhaus, Hausbaum), and ends with the skill check. Speak tasks let the child say a Quatschsatz or a swapped word aloud; they are practice only, so the skill check marks the games a screen can mark (real or Quatsch, swapped sounds, syllables and word parts). Tongue twisters have their own set (tongue-twisters). Every Quatschwort and Quatschsatz is made up for Twist.

## C, Y, X, äu, ck und ß (C, Y, X, äu, ck and ß)

`de-DE.lit-de.letters-c-y-x-aeu-ck-ss` teaches `lit-de.letters.c-y-x-aeu-ck-ss` in de-DE, klasse-1. Ages 6-7, about 10 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

The last letter group of Klasse 1: rare letters and spellings the child meets in reading. Lesson 1: ck is read as k and comes after a short vowel (Socke, Glocke); ß is read as s and is not a B (Fuß, groß). Lesson 2: äu sounds like eu and comes from au (Maus, Mäuse; Baum, Bäume); C is often read as k (Clown), Y at the end of a word as i (Baby, Pony), X as ks (Hexe, Taxi). Lesson 3 reads words with all six and ends with the skill check. Choosing between k and ck by rule is left to the later spelling skill; here ck is offered against k and kk in short familiar words.

|---|---|---|---|

## Die Buchstaben E, N, D und U (The letters E, N, D and U)

`de-DE.lit-de.letters-e-n-d-u` teaches `lit-de.letters.e-n-d-u` in de-DE, klasse-1. Ages 6-7, about 10 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

The third letter group in Fibel order. One lesson each for E, N, D and U: hear the sound, find it in words, see and trace the letter, practised in three stages. Each lesson sets the new sound against its nearest neighbour: E against I, N against M, D against T, U against O (Mund and Mond). Lesson 5 reads words made only of known letters (Nase, Ente, Sonne, Tanne, Mond, Mund) and ends with the skill check. Writing the letters is practised in Practise (tracing and copying); the skill check marks hearing the sounds and reading the words.

## Die Anlauttabelle (The sound chart)

`de-DE.lit-de.sound-chart` teaches `lit-de.letters.sound-chart` in de-DE, klasse-1. Ages 6-7, about 10 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

Using an Anlauttabelle before the letters are taught one by one. Each field of the chart is a letter with a picture whose word starts with that letter's sound (M wie Maus). Lesson 1: hear a sound or a word, find the chart picture that starts the same, and with it the letter; keep the sound apart from the letter name (Elefant does not start with L) and from sounds later in the word. Lesson 2 goes through a whole short word sound by sound (Hut: H wie Hund, U wie Uhr, T wie Tisch), puts the chart pictures in order and ends with the skill check. The Learn screens show a small chart (sound-chart, six fields) with the field being talked about marked, and Oma as the three fields O, M, A. Tasks that ask for a sound's field show a short chart of four fields with every option on it and nothing marked, so the child has to find the field; l1-s1 shows one letter as a gap with two options that are not on the chart. Pictures are always named, so each field's word starts with exactly its sound (no Ohr for O, no Elefant for L). Sorting bins and options also carry fields, and tapping one says it ("M wie Maus").

## Schreibschrift, große Buchstaben (Joined script, capital letters)

`de-DE.lit-de.joined-capitals` teaches `lit-de.handwriting.joined-capitals` in de-DE, klasse-2. Ages 6-7, about 12 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

Children write the capital letters in Schreibschrift and go on from them into the small letters of the word. Lesson 1 sets out where the capitals live (from the line up to the Dach) and when a word starts with one (Satzanfang, Nomen, Namen); lesson 2 joins a capital to the rest of the word, and where a capital is not joined, sets the next letter close beside it so the word stays together; it ends with the skill check. Every writing-lines task uses `script: joined`, so the child sees the model in the school's Ausgangsschrift (SAS, LA, VA or Grundschrift, a setting) and can see where a capital joins on. Which capitals join differs between these scripts, so the lesson teaches only what holds in all of them: some capitals join on and some do not, the child follows the model on the lines, and the one capital named as not joining is O, which ends at the top in SAS, LA and VA. Word options for "which word do you write with a capital" are shown in small letters, so the capital does not give the answer away. The skill check marks what a screen can mark: how high a capital goes, which words start with one, small letters after it and the next letter set close beside; writing the letters themselves is practised in Practise with the tracing tasks.

Children write the small letters in Schreibschrift and join them, so a word is written in one go without lifting the pen. Lesson 1 joins at the bottom: most small letters end low and the joining stroke runs up into the next letter (im, mein, lila); lesson 2 joins at the top after o, w, v and b, sets i-Punkte, Umlaut-Punkte and t-Striche once the word is finished, and ends with the skill check. Tracing and copying on writing lines teach the joins; choice, sorting and true or false tasks check what the child knows about them. No task names one Ausgangsschrift: the joins taught (most letters end low, o, w, v and b end high) hold for the joined scripts German schools use. The player still draws the writing lines in print, so no task says the child can see a join; the spoken text describes the movement instead. Writing the letters and words themselves is practised in the tracing and copying tasks of Practise; the skill check marks what a screen can mark: writing a word in one go, where a join starts, and dots and strokes last.

Lesson 1 learns that a figure is punktsymmetrisch when it looks the same after a half turn about its centre, and checks letters, digits and short words (N, S, Z, H, X, 8, 69, SOS ja; A, T, M, 6 nein), keeping it apart from having a Symmetrieachse; lesson 2 checks shapes (Rechteck, Quadrat, Kreis, Sechseck, schiefes Parallelogramm ja; Dreieck nein), sorts letters, and ends with the skill check. Turning a drawn figure on screen to check waits for a rotate task.


| Lesson | New | Tasks | Activities |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Gleich nach einer halben Drehung | yes | 20 | warm-up, learn, practise (5 full, 5 some, 5 none), check (quick, 3 of 6) |
| 2. Punktsymmetrische Figuren | yes | 22 | warm-up, learn, practise (5 full, 5 some, 5 none), check (skill, 5 of 20) |

Task types: multiple_choice 22, true_false 30, image_multiple_choice 4, sorting 4. Builds on: `math.symmetry.several-axes`, `math.space.mental-moves`. Misconceptions addressed: 2.

## Römische Zahlen (Roman numerals)

`de-DE.math.roman-numerals` teaches `math.large-numbers.roman-numerals` in de-DE, klasse-4. Ages 8-10, about 12 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

Lesson 1 reads and writes römische Zahlzeichen to 20 with I, V and X: a smaller sign to the right of a bigger one adds, one to the left subtracts (IV, IX), and no sign stands more than three times in a row. Lesson 2 adds L and C, reads numbers to 100 in parts (tens, then ones), reads the hours on a clock face with Roman numerals, compares the Roman way with our Stellenwertsystem (an X is always ten, there is no zero) and ends with the skill check. The voice never reads a Roman numeral aloud, and Roman options are not read, so the child must read them.

|---|---|---|---|
| 1. I, V und X | yes | 20 | warm-up, learn, practise (5 full, 5 some, 5 none in context), check (quick, 3 of 6) |

Task types: multiple_choice 31, text_input 18, true_false 9, matching 2. Builds on: `math.numbers-to-1000.place-value`. Misconceptions addressed: 4.

Lesson 1 takes the diagonal join: a letter that ends on the line joins up and across to the next one (in, an, um, and to a tall letter in il, ch, at). Every writing-lines task uses `script: joined`, so the model follows the school's handwriting scheme, which is a setting; tasks teach only what holds in every scheme. The app does not yet check the child's own joins: any ink counts. The skill check marks knowing the joins; Practise covers writing them.

Every practise stage and both checks also ask the child to set the hands to a quarter hour (clock_hands_drag).

## Gut lesbar verbunden schreiben (Neat, joined handwriting)

`en-GB.lit-en.joined-legible` teaches `lit-en.handwriting.joined-legible` in en-GB, year-3. Ages 8-10, about 13 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

Children make their joined handwriting easy to read. Lesson 1 takes size and slope: small letters the same height, tall letters reaching higher, tails going below the line, and downstrokes that are parallel (all leaning the same way). Lesson 2 takes spacing: even gaps between letters, a clear gap between words, and joining whole words and short phrases neatly; it ends with the skill check. Every writing-lines task uses `script: joined`, so the model follows the school's handwriting scheme, a setting; tasks teach only what holds in every scheme. Capitals are left unjoined in this lesson, and Learn says that many schools do this and the teacher shows the school's own way. The app does not yet judge the size, slope or spacing of the child's own writing: any ink counts, so the skill check uses choice tasks on size, slope, spacing and what makes writing legible, and Practise covers the writing itself.

Lesson 1 tells a curve (a line that bends), a straight line (it never bends and in maths goes on for ever) and a line segment (straight, with two end points) apart, in words, letters, shapes on squared paper and things around us; lesson 2 measures line segments on a ruler in cm and mm, also when the segment does not start at 0, compares lengths given in cm and mm, and ends with the skill check. Drawing a line segment of a given length, and pictures of curves to choose from, wait for a drawing task and a curve component.

## Wörtliche Rede vollständig zeichensetzen (Punctuating direct speech fully)

`en-GB.lit-en.direct-speech-full` teaches `lit-en.grammar.direct-speech-full` in en-GB, year-4. Ages 8-10, about 14 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

Direct speech needs more than inverted commas. When the reporting clause comes first, it ends with a comma, and the spoken words start with a capital letter: Mum said, “Time for bed.” The end punctuation goes inside the inverted commas. When the speech comes first, a comma replaces the full stop inside the inverted commas: “Time for bed,” said Mum. Lesson 1 punctuates speech after the reporting clause; lesson 2 puts the speech first, keeps question and exclamation marks, and ends with the skill check.

Lesson 1 plans a class survey: a clear question that fits what you want to know, answer choices with "something else" for the rest, the right people to ask (every child once, not only your friends), tally marks to collect the answers, and the steps in order. Lesson 2 counts the tally marks into a table, checks that the total matches the number of children asked, picks the bar chart that fits, says the result in a sentence the data supports (9 of 24 children, not "everyone"), and ends with the skill check. Asking real classmates and drawing the chart by hand stay in the classroom.

Punctuation from Appendix 2 of the National Curriculum for Year 5. Lesson 1 takes parenthesis: extra information added to a sentence inside a pair of brackets, a pair of dashes or a pair of commas, and the test that the sentence still makes sense without it. Lesson 1 calls a game fair when every player has the same number of ways to win, counted on one dice or one spinner (Zoe 1, 2, 3 and Ravi 4, 5, 6: 3 ways each, fair; one colour each on a spinner with three red sectors and one blue: not fair), and changes a rule to make a game fair. Lesson 2 counts the ways with two coins (HH, HT, TH, TT: one of each happens two ways) and two dice (a total of 7 six ways, 12 one way, 3 + 4 and 4 + 3 counted apart), decides whether games with them are fair, and ends with the skill check. Playing the games in the app waits for an experiment task.

|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Gewinnmöglichkeiten zählen | yes | 20 | warm-up, learn, practise (5 full, 5 some, 5 none), check (quick, 3 of 6) |
| 2. Zwei Münzen und zwei Würfel | yes | 22 | warm-up, learn, practise (5 full, 5 some, 5 none), check (skill, 5 of 20) |

Task types: multiple_choice 36, true_false 17, text_input 6, image_multiple_choice 1. Builds on: `math.chance.compare-chances`, `math.chance.combinations`. Misconceptions addressed: 2.

## Brüche bei Größen (Fractions of measures)

`en-GB.math.fractions-measures` teaches `math.fractions.everyday-measures` in en-GB, year-5. Ages 8-10, about 12 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

Lesson 1 turns half, quarter and three quarters of an hour into minutes and of a metre into centimetres: first the whole in the smaller unit (1 hour = 60 minutes, 1 m = 100 cm), then divide by 4 for a quarter and take three of them for three quarters, with a circle and a bar as the model; lesson 2 does the same for litres and kilograms (¼ l = 250 ml, ¾ kg = 750 g), adds one and a half, and ends with the skill check. Each unit keeps its own whole, so ½ hour is 30 minutes and not 50.

## Semikolon, Doppelpunkt und Gedankenstrich (Semicolons, colons and dashes)

`en-GB.lit-en.semicolons-colons` teaches `lit-en.grammar.semicolons-colons` in en-GB, year-6. Ages 8-10, about 15 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

A semicolon joins two independent clauses that are closely linked (It was raining; we stayed inside). A colon comes after a complete clause to introduce a list, or before a clause that explains the first. A dash can also join two clauses, less formally. Lesson 1 works on semicolons between clauses and the comma splice; lesson 2 on colons for lists and explanations, on semicolons that split a list of longer items with commas inside (a colon introduces the list, semicolons go between the items, and the last item takes "and"), and on dashes, and ends with the skill check. The record writes the dash as a spaced hyphen ( - ), because record text carries no dash characters; the app shows a proper dash.


| Lesson | New | Tasks | Activities |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Das Semikolon | yes | 20 | warm-up, learn, practise (5 full, 5 some, 5 none), check (quick, 3 of 6) |

Task types: multiple_choice 32, true_false 10, fill_in_blank 13, highlight_in_text 2, sorting 3. Builds on: `lit-en.grammar.parenthesis`. Misconceptions addressed: 4.

## Synonyme und Antonyme (Synonyms and antonyms)

`en-GB.lit-en.synonyms-antonyms` teaches `lit-en.grammar.synonyms-antonyms` in en-GB, year-6. Ages 8-10, about 13 minutes a lesson. Status: draft, version 1.

Synonyms are words with the same or a similar meaning (big, large); antonyms are words with opposite meanings (ancient, modern). A synonym or antonym is the same word class as the word it pairs with, and many antonyms are made with a prefix (happy, unhappy). Lesson 1 sorts and matches synonyms and antonyms; lesson 2 makes antonyms with prefixes, checks word class and shades of meaning, and ends with the skill check.
